Hi Eddy / Marcus / Team,

Thanks for raising this. We've completed the proration audit for the `acme-enterprise-connector` SKU for September 2026. Summary below and a CSV with per-usage rows is attached.

Summary:
- Proration is applied at the SKU × PayerID level based on usage timestamps.
- Acme had multiple payer IDs active in September; the migration on 2026-09-14 resulted in 60.3% of usage attributed to payer ID 555-ACME-EU after the cutover.
- The original invoice was generated to the legacy payer (555-ACME-US) because the invoice generation job ran before the migration flag propagated to our invoice index. This caused the full-month line to appear on the invoice.
- We have created a Settlement Adjustment (SA-2026-0914-ACME) that will credit $10,970.40 to Acme US and create a corresponding charge to Acme EU so the net allocation reflects actual usage. The adjustment will post with the next payout cycle on 2026-11-05.

VAT / Tax notes:
- The adjustment will be issued as a net settlement (no VAT charged on the credit). For EU VAT treatment, please consult your tax advisor; the invoice metadata will include the original VAT flags for each payer.

Attachments: aws_proration_audit_2026-09.csv (contains: timestamp, usage_id, sku, payer_id, units, unit_price, line_total)

If Acme requires an earlier cash adjustment (e.g., to avoid withholding payment), we can issue a provisional credit memo within 48 hours after confirming payer identification. Let us know which route you prefer.

Regards,
Marketplace Billing Support — AWS
